extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent agents and attorneys), respondents in USPTO OED disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO enforcement staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order approving a proposed settlement resolving an OED disciplinary complaint against a registered patent practitioner, setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, sanctions, and procedures for noncompliance under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement Agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. §11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement must set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. §11.26; upon approval it resolves the Office's disciplinary action arising from those stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a settlement that clearly states stipulated facts, admissions of violations (if any), and proposed discipline; obtain approval from the USPTO Director or designate to finalize and resolve disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for practitioner discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner discipline pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.26; registered practitioners are subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §10.20 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO must comply with USPTO disciplinary rules and may be subject to OED proceedings under the cited statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting papers containing false representations (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting papers to the Office that contain a false representation of ownership (or other false statements) violates 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: filing a 'Statement Under 37 C.F.R. 3.73(b)' that represents the client is assignee of the entire interest when the client is assignee of only 98% constitutes a violation even if there is no intent to mislead; practitioners must ensure accuracy of ownership representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of adequate preparation before filing (37 C.F.R. §10.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing papers with the Office without preparation adequate under the circumstances violates 37 C.F.R. §10.77(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must research and verify relevant facts (e.g., assignment records, litigation status) before filing; reliance on another attorney's statements without sufficient verification may be inadequate and lead to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to research and verify facts before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must research issues and verify whether, under known facts, papers can properly be filed with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to investigate ownership records or the existence of litigation over ownership (even if a colleague indicates a position) can constitute inadequate preparation and support disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing method and transmission certification (37 C.F.R. §1.8 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by facsimile should be transmitted under Certificates of Transmission under 37 C.F.R. §1.8 bearing the practitioner's signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure transmission certificates comply with the applicable rule and bear the appropriate signature when filing by facsimile or other permitted means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party petition standing limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may dismiss petitions by third parties for lack of standing or insufficient basis to permit third-party action regarding another's patent application; the USPTO is not the appropriate forum for resolving ownership disputes between private parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership disputes (e.g., contested percent interests) are generally not resolved in the USPTO and may require litigation in appropriate courts; practitioners should not use USPTO procedures as a substitute for proper fora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction structure: suspension with stay and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline may include a suspension from practice (here, six months) that is stayed in its entirety, coupled with a probationary period (here, six months) with specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stayed suspension means the suspension is not immediately served but may be imposed if probation terms are violated; probation duration and conditions should be clearly stated in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictive condition: prohibition on signing Office papers
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of discipline, the practitioner may be prohibited from signing (electronically or otherwise) any paper filed in the Office for a specified period (here, six months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction may be absolute for the period specified; the order may allow limited activities (e.g., use of PKI to transmit documents signed by others) and should state precise scope and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited PKI/electronic-use allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may be permitted to use their Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificate number to electronically mail papers to the Office that have been signed by other registered practitioners, despite other signing restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that limited electronic transmission of others' signed documents may be allowed even when the practitioner is barred from signing Office filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of discipline and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director will publish the Final Order and a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the violation(s) and discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published notice will include factual summary and regulatory citations; publication is part of the sanction and public notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. §11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the States where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED must communicate discipline to relevant state bars/courts; practitioners should expect cross-jurisdictional notification following public discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause process for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply with probation conditions, the Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, mail it to the practitioner's last address of record, and afford fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order to Show Cause triggers further proceedings; the practitioner's response is considered before OED may request suspension from the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for seeking immediate suspension upon noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 15-day response period, if OED remains of the opinion that the practitioner failed to comply, OED shall deliver to the USPTO Director (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) the practitioner's response, and (iii) evidence supporting the opinion, and request imposition of an immediate suspension of up to six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED's submission to the USPTO Director may prompt immediate suspension; the record submitted should document the alleged probationary violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate suspension not stayed by review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director suspends the practitioner pursuant to the Final Order and the practitioner seeks review of that decision, such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the immediate suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should understand that appealing a suspension does not automatically stay the suspension; the suspension takes effect immediately as ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension (37 C.F.R. §11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended during any portion of the probationary period, the practitioner must comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 (duties of a suspended practitioner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize with §11.58 obligations (e.g., notification to clients, transfer of files) and ensure compliance during any period of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrent suspension potential and non-exclusivity of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order may permit multiple suspensions during the probationary period and does not preclude the Office from seeking discipline for the same misconduct in other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners may be suspended multiple times under the order for repeated or continued noncompliance; the Office can pursue other disciplinary actions for the same misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered in addressing any further complaint or similar misconduct and may be used: (a) as an aggravating factor in determining future discipline, and/or (b) to rebut statements made on the practitioner's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary history can enhance sanctions or be used against a practitioner in later matters; settlement terms will be part of that record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and the Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can specify that each side pays its own costs rather than awarding costs to the Office or seeking reimbursement.
